dominant_strengths: Bold oversized headline with tight leading anchors the hero confidently and signals a modern, design-forward product voice
Clean nav system with clear hierarchy, dropdown affordances, and a recognizable teal CTA aligned to brand identity
Smart promo card placement above the fold introduces a feature without disrupting the headline's dominance
dominant_weaknesses: Headline-on-white feels generic for a motion-first brand — ironically static, with no visible animation cue or kinetic affordance in the hero
Teal CTA, pink Motion Tokens icon, and orange promo illustration create three competing accent hues without a unifying palette logic
Feature cards at the bottom feel templated and disconnected from the hero composition; spacing and alignment read more landing-page-default than crafted
fix_priorities: Embed a live Lottie animation in the hero to embody the 'designs come alive' promise rather than asserting it in text
Tighten the accent palette — pick one secondary hue and let icons share a system rather than each card owning a different color
Rework feature row into a more intentional grid with stronger typographic rhythm and visual relationship to the hero
rationale.norman_balance: Behaviorally clear and navigable, but visceral impact is muted for a motion brand and reflective payoff is weak — it tells rather than shows.
rationale.intent_fit: Functions as a competent LottieFiles marketing page but underdelivers on the core brief of demonstrating motion as the product's soul.
